validator: draft 1 passes validate.mjs with no problems, soft points or warnings. The faults below are the critic's, not the validator's.
keep: The idea is named in one line up front: a radian is the angle whose arc is one radius long [1], so an angle in radians is a count of radius-lengths, and a full turn is 2π [2].

The picture is the brief's: the radius lifted off as a bendy rod and laid round the edge, counted in radius-lengths, with a size handle that leaves the count alone (Moore's arc-length design, notes 4.3, 6.1).

Why the radian has no length unit is taught from the picture (arc ÷ radius, both lengths), while still calling it a unit of angle, so it does not feed Moore's 'not a unit of angle measure' (notes 6.1).
2π comes from the circumference 2πr that Geometry fundamentals taught, not handed over; 180° = π [2] and 57.3° are computed from it.
Arc length s = rθ is derived from the definition, and the Pearson slips (degrees in rθ, θr²) each have a DO screen, the second checked by its unit.

Misconceptions from the brief each have a DO screen with its own wrong answer: the whole circle as one radian (screen 6, 0.25), radians tied to the circle's size (screens 2 and 4), the wrong mode (screen 12), the conversion the wrong way (screen 8), and the rev/min slips (screen 13).
Fourteen screens alternate SHOW 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 with DO 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and close on three mixed puzzles, as i4 did.
P = Tω, the radian-mode convention and the calculus line are not in RESEARCH and are written as 'Textbooks add that', unfootnoted.
fix: Causal step skipped: 'Every point of the edge is twice as far from the centre, so the arc between the same two arms doubles too' asserts the arc doubles without the reason. Give it: a circle twice as big is the same shape at twice the scale, as in lesson 1, so every length in it doubles, the arc as well as the radius.
Interactive brief shows the effect, not the cause: it names the count staying put but not why. Name the rod growing with the circle, so the cause (rod and arc scale together) is what he watches.
False absolute in practice: 'the radian figure is much smaller than the degree figure' fails at 0°, where both are 0. Say that for any angle but zero the radian figure is about 57.3 times smaller.

Weak distractor on screen 12: 0.878 (the cosine) is not a slip anyone is reported to make. Use 0.5, the angle itself, whose hint teaches the real difference: the arc is 0.5 radius-lengths but the tip's height, the sine, is a little less.

Unreadable at 340 px: screen 7 sets two arms 'side by side' on separate circles. Draw both on one circle, 10° solid and 10 radians dashed, with the 10-radian path drawn as a spiral that wraps 1.59 times, so the two stopping points are seen together.
Screen 4 draws a 1 m and a 3 m circle side by side; at 340 px the small one is tiny. Stack them, one above the other, each labelled with its radius and arc.

Thin linking: the explain says 'lesson 3's turning arm' but never says the arm's angle is the angle measured. Add that the angle is the one between the arm's starting position and where it has turned to, as in Round the circle.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 with these seven fixes; nothing structural changes.
